reason: The issue names the cause and proposes the fix: do the retry backoff on the driver side (progress.wait) instead of an in-page setTimeout. Any driver-side wait lets the retry loop continue and click after the cover goes, so it passes; the error-message alternative does not fix the stated expected behaviour and is not a full fix.

deciding_assertions: browser_cookie_set and browser_cookie_get: error must contain 'Cannot infer the cookie domain from the page URL "about:blank", specify "domain".'
reason: The issue gives the expected message 'Cannot infer cookie domain from current page URL "about:blank". Please specify "domain".' The test checks a different exact text. A fix that uses the issue's own message, or any other normal wording, fails stringContaining.

deciding_assertions: tool error exits with non-zero code: 'click e999' in text mode and in --json mode both exit with code 1, and the output still holds the error / isError true
reason: The title reports exit status 0 on isError as the bug, and the issue asks for a non-zero exit in both text and JSON modes. The narrowest fix sets the exit code to 1 when the tool result has isError, and exit code 1 is the normal convention for a failed command, so it passes. The issue's other option (only document status 0) is not a code fix of the reported bug, so I do not count it as a competing behaviour.

deciding_assertions: library.spec createConnection detaches backend listeners from a caller owned context (listener counts on context 'close' and browser 'disconnected' return to the start value after browser_close); createConnection drops its connection to an attached browser when the backend is disposed (open proxy connections go to 0 after browser_close)
reason: The issue asks only that browser_close clear the cached backendPromise so a shared-context HTTP client gets a fresh backend. The narrowest fix (emit disconnected or clear the cache on explicit close) fixes that case, but it does not remove the listeners or close the connection to a remote browser, so it fails both fail-to-pass tests. The issue's own two-client case is not in either test list.

deciding_assertions: should roundtrip IndexedDB Map and Set with newContext / setStorageState: the restored values are a Map [['mk','mv']] and a Set [1,2], and storageState is stable over the round trip; p2p page-evaluate tests: evaluate of a Map or Set still gives {}
reason: The issue's own case and both restore entry points follow from the issue. The issue says the evaluate path that turns Map and Set into {} is intentional and out of scope, and an existing test already checks it for arguments. So the narrowest reasonable fix adds Map and Set support only for the IndexedDB storage path, and it passes the new evaluate assertions. A global serializer change would break existing behaviour that the issue says to keep.

deciding_assertions: cli-navigation.spec 'reload with alert during load': the CLI reload command must return with the modal state for an alert during load
reason: The issue reports only browser_navigate and names Tab.navigate() as the place to add the modal-state race. The narrowest fix wraps page.goto in Tab.navigate with _raceAgainstModalStates and passes 'alert dialog during navigation'. The reload tool calls page.reload directly, so that fix does not cover reload and the reload test fails. Reload is a separate tool that the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: parseLocator within: all four languages parse to 'internal:role=row >> internal:chain="internal:role=cell >> nth=2"'; parseLocator getByRef: all four languages parse to 'aria-ref=e5'
reason: The issue gives both method names in all four languages and the target selectors (b >> internal:chain="a", aria-ref=e5). The exact strings follow from the existing selector stringifier. A fix that adds the methods to the four tables with that mapping passes.

deciding_assertions: browsers-path.spec: with process.platform faked to 'android', require(playwright-core) prints PLAYWRIGHT_CORE_LOADED with no 'Unsupported platform', both for PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0 and for an explicit path
reason: The issue asks that Playwright run on Android/Termux when PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH is set (0 or an explicit path), as in 1.58.2, with no eager platform check. A fix that makes the default cache directory lazy passes. To fix the issue's stated case, a fix must also defer the other eager copies of the platform check that run on import (serverRegistry, CLI daemon dir), which a search for the error text finds. A fix that only touches the registry copy would leave the issue's case broken, so it is not a correct fix.

deciding_assertions: should recover tracing after a failed stop (stop to a path under a file fails, then a new start/stop records a valid trace); should release the stack session when saving the trace fails (stacks dir is removed after the failed stop)
reason: The issue reports broken traces after a page crash and suggests several options (surface the crash, a context reset tool, investigate). It never mentions a failed tracing.stop or the stack session. The tests check recovery after a failed save, a case and code path that no reasonable fix of the stated crash scenario must cover.

deciding_assertions: should keep the rest of Temporal intact (new test, passes before): Object.prototype.toString(Temporal.Now) is '[object Temporal.Now]' and Object.keys(Temporal) plus Object.keys(Temporal.Now) is []
reason: The fail-to-pass tests (fixed time for all five Now methods, advance with the clock, system time zone by default) follow from the issue. The new property-attribute check does not: a reasonable fix in the createIntl shape that the issue points to, or one that builds the fake with Object.create plus assignment, adds enumerable own keys or loses the toStringTag and fails. The issue only says the rest of Temporal stays functionally untouched; it does not ask to keep property descriptors.

deciding_assertions: should only return cookies that apply to the url (browser context and global request): host-only, .domain and Path=/foo/ cookies are filtered by RFC 6265 domain-match and path-match for /api, /api/x, /apiv2, sub host, notfoo host, /foo, /foo/, /foo/bar; changed p2p test uses .one.com for the subdomain cookie
reason: The issue states each case (host-only exact match, path segment boundary, Path=/foo/ not for /foo), cites the RFC rules, names filterCookies as the shared code for browserContext.cookies and the request context, and gives the fix. Any fix of filterCookies and pathMatches with those rules passes every assertion, and the p2p send test stays green.

deciding_assertions: test_union_mixed_date_timestamp: union keeps date(2001,1,1) and Timestamp('2001-01-01') as two distinct object-level values; also asserts a Pandas4Warning matching 'Inferring datetime64 from data containing datetime.date objects'
reason: The issue names two acceptable outcomes: treat the values as different (preferred) or as identical, and only asks that the exception go away. A fix that treats them as identical (cast the date level to datetime64 and merge) is offered by the issue and fails the expected two-value object level; the fix that keeps them distinct passes. The warning check also depends on the union result being rebuilt through the existing inference path.

deciding_assertions: test_replace_dict_inplace_memory: ser.replace(dict of 2000 keys, inplace=True) peak traced memory < n*n//4; test_replace_small_dict_inplace_memory: peak < ser nbytes
reason: The issue reports a TypeError for a non-inplace replace with a large dict; the real fix only changes the inplace path, so the issue's case already works, and the tests measure peak memory of inplace=True replace against thresholds the issue never mentions. A fix aimed at the TypeError does nothing for these memory limits.

deciding_assertions: test_series_all_null_not_datetime: read_json('{"a": null}', typ='series') equals Series([nan], index=['a']) (float64); pyarrow variant gives null[pyarrow]; test_series_all_nan_roundtrip over all orients
reason: Narrowest reasonable fix: do not run date conversion on an all-null Series in the series parser; the existing object-to-float coercion then gives float NaN, which passes all three tests (the round trip and the pyarrow backend are direct variants of the same input). The issue asks for None rather than NaT, but NaN is the normal missing value after the existing coercion, so a fix that stops the date conversion meets the expected value; a fix that forces object None would be a further change of existing coercion.

deciding_assertions: test_cummin_max_nan_with_mask_propagates[cummin/cummax]: groupby cummin/cummax on a Float64 array with an unmasked NaN propagates NaN; also min/max added to test_groupby_reductions_dont_skip_nan_with_mask (NaN mixed with values propagates)
reason: The issue reports groupby min/max (and agg min/max) giving inf for NaN in a nullable float column. The tests also require cummin/cummax to propagate NaN, a different operation and kernel that the issue never mentions; a fix in group_min_max alone (or in the min/max post-processing) leaves the four cumulative tests failing.

deciding_assertions: test_cached_accessor_deprecation: `from pandas.core.accessor import CachedAccessor` must emit Pandas4Warning matching 'CachedAccessor is deprecated', and CachedAccessor is accessor.Accessor
reason: The issue asks for a warning when CachedAccessor is used, but gives neither the warning class nor when it fires. A reasonable fix that warns with FutureWarning/DeprecationWarning, or that warns on instantiation through a subclass wrapper, fails the Pandas4Warning-on-import check or the identity check; only a module __getattr__ with Pandas4Warning passes.

deciding_assertions: test_where_series_listlike_other_wrong_length and changed SetitemCastingEquivalents: wrong-length list raises ValueError 'Length of values (3) does not match length of index (4)' instead of the numpy broadcast error; test_where_tuple_other_numeric_ea / _bool: tuples lined up for numeric EA dtypes; test_index_where_listlike_other_keeps_ea_dtype: Index.where/putmask
reason: The issue asks that DataFrame[str].where(mask, ['cudf']) keep StringDtype. The tests also change the error for wrong-length lists to a new message, change tuple handling for numeric and bool EA dtypes, and cover Index.where/putmask. A fix that only keeps the string dtype for a length-1 list other passes the issue's case but fails these tests.

deciding_assertions: test_eval_int64_result_dtype_type: df['c'].dtype.type is np.int64 after eval with numexpr; test_result_dtype_type_matches_numpy[int64]: Series arithmetic and where through the numexpr expressions module give dtype.type np.int64
reason: The issue reports that select_dtypes drops a column made by df.eval. A fix in select_dtypes (match by dtype equality) fails the dtype.type assertion; a fix that normalizes only the eval engine result fails the second test, which covers Series arithmetic and where via pandas.core.computation.expressions, entry points the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: test_timedelta_with_na_group_key (cumsum/cummin/cummax, units), test_datetime_cummin_max_with_na_group_key (tz None/UTC, units), test_period_cummin_max_with_na_group_key, test_rank_datetimelike_with_na_group_key (na_option keep/top/bottom), test_datetime_cummax_no_precision_loss_with_na_group_key
reason: The issue names the cause and the fix: do not cast datetimelike int64 values to float64 for transforms with dropped NA keys, and fill the dropped rows with NaT. A fix that passes is_datetimelike into _get_cython_vals and fills the output with iNaT covers timedelta, datetime (tz-aware), period (same datetimelike path), all units, and rank with every na_option; these are direct variants of the stated cases.

deciding_assertions: test_loc_setitem_with_expansion_length1_ea_single_cell: df.loc[0,'b'] = [Timestamp tz / Period / Interval] must unpack to the scalar and give an EA column, not store the list
reason: The issue asks that a list set into a single cell of a new column be stored as the list itself. A fix that follows this rule for all list-likes stores [Timestamp] as a list and fails the EA test; a fix that only handles object/string values leaves the EA case failing as before. The unpacking rule for length-1 EA scalars is a design choice the issue does not state.

deciding_assertions: test_is_setitem_syntax_in_caller_frame: calls com.is_setitem_syntax_in_caller_frame() and expects [True, True, False, False]; test_setitem_not_through_subscript_syntax: df['a'].__setitem__(0, 100) emits no warning
reason: The test calls a new helper name pandas.core.common.is_setitem_syntax_in_caller_frame that the issue does not give. The issue also lists several possible approaches (detect Cython, analyse stack frames, or make it a warning with an option), and the tests need the frame-opcode approach.

deciding_assertions: test_precision_float_index_names: repr(ser.rename(0.55555555)) must not contain '0.55555555' (Series name footer 'Name: ...'); test_to_html_column_index_named_zero: column index named 0 shows '<th>0</th>' in to_html
reason: The issue covers float index names in DataFrame display. A fix that formats index and column-index names with display.precision passes the DataFrame parts but leaves the Series name footer ('Name: 0.55555555') unformatted, and it need not fix the separate falsy-name bug (name 0 rendered empty in to_html); both cases are not in the issue.

deciding_assertions: test_needs_python_regex_unicode_classes / test_needs_python_regex_unsupported_code: call arr._needs_python_regex(pat); (?=test)+, (?=test)*, (?=test)?, (?:a(?=b))+ now expected True; test_replace_lookarounds new case (?:a(?=b))+
reason: Many fail-to-pass tests call the new method name _needs_python_regex (renamed from _has_unsupported_regex), which the issue never gives. The tests also require lookarounds inside repeats to be detected, a case outside the issue's Unicode character-class report. A fix that falls back to Python re for \w/\d/\s/\b passes the behaviour tests but fails these.

deciding_assertions: test_remove_where_filter_and_condition[100]: where='index in selector and A>=50' must remove only rows that match both parts; the issue's own case (test_remove_where_many_selectors[100], pure 'index in [many]') is pass-to-pass
reason: The issue's case, remove with a long 'index in [...]' list, already works before the fix: the many-selectors test passes before and after. The failing test combines the post-read filter with a numexpr condition, which the issue never mentions. A fix limited to the issue's case would already be in place and would not touch this path.

deciding_assertions: test_datetime_and_object_nat_no_dtype_check: Series([NaT]) datetime64 vs object NaT with check_exact=True must be equal; test_ea_and_object_na_no_dtype_check[*-True]: NA in numeric EA vs object NA equal in both orders, and NA vs object nan must raise 'Series are different'
reason: The numeric EA cases are direct variants of the issue's Int32 example, and the NA vs nan raise follows the related GH#18463 rule and the check_exact=False path. The datetime64 NaT vs object NaT test is a different dtype family and missing value that the issue does not state. A fix limited to masked (nullable numeric) arrays solves the issue but fails that test.

deciding_assertions: test_maybe_box_native complex64/complex128 -> complex; test_to_dict_returns_native_types data3 (complex columns must give complex); test_to_dict_complex_native[object, Sparse[complex128]]
reason: The issue is about numpy.bool_ in to_dict of object Series; maybe_box_native already boxes bools before the fix (the bool column in data3 and the obj8-bool case are not what fail). All failing assertions are about complex numbers, which the issue never mentions.

deciding_assertions: test_pad_backfill_axis_1_inplace[ffill/bfill, 1/columns]: result is df, and df equals the filled frame
reason: The test is the issue's own example for both methods and both axis spellings the issue names. The narrowest fix, updating self in place and returning self in the axis=1 branch, passes every assertion.

deciding_assertions: test_float_inf_raises / test_to_timedelta_object_inf: Timedelta(inf) and to_timedelta(inf) raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta match 'without overflow', coerce gives NaT; test_round_float_overflow_unit: Timedelta(1e19, unit='s') and Timedelta(10**19, unit='s') raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta 'without overflow'
reason: The issue asks for a microsecond default unit for numeric input to Timestamp/Timedelta. The tests check error handling of non-finite and overflowing floats, which the issue does not mention, and they match a message the issue does not give. A fix of the unit default does not touch these assertions.

deciding_assertions: test_online_vs_non_online_mean[obj1]: single-column DataFrame online ewm mean (and its update path) equals the non-online ewm mean
reason: The issue names the single-column case, the expected result (agree with .mean()), and both faulty lines. The narrowest fix, deltas sized by row count and indexed by the row index, passes the parametrized comparison for every flag combination.

deciding_assertions: test_concat_timedeltaindex_freq_order_independent[True]: TimedeltaIndex freq='2D' concat [s1,s3,s2] with sort=True must keep freq; also test_concat_datetimeindex_freq_order_independent[True/None] and test_constructor_dict_of_series_datetimeindex_freq
reason: The datetime CustomBusinessDay cases (default sort, explicit sort=True, DataFrame from dict) are the issue's case or direct variants. The TimedeltaIndex test with a regular inferable freq and explicit sort=True is a case the issue does not state; the issue even says regular freqs work. A fix that restores the shared freq for DatetimeIndex in the union path solves the issue but fails that test.

deciding_assertions: test_strftime_year_lt_1000: '%Y%%Y' -> '0064%Y' and '%%q' -> '%q' (escaped directives); test_strftime_escaped_n_no_warning: '%%n' gives no deprecation warning and literal '%n'
reason: The issue asks for zero-padded years in str(Period) (and so in %Y). Padding %Y in custom strftime formats is a fair variant, but the tests also require correct handling of escaped '%%q', '%%Y' and '%%n', and no warning for '%%n'. These are separate escaping bugs that the issue does not mention; a fix that only pads %Y fails them.

deciding_assertions: test_string_multiindex_level_literal_nan(_append), test_string_multiindex_level_literal_and_real_na, test_string_index_literal_nan_then_real_na_append, test_string_index_append_value_colliding_with_sentinel_raises (ValueError match 'collides with the sentinel')
reason: The issue's case, a plain string Index with a literal 'nan' through to_hdf, already round-trips before the fix (the string-index literal-nan tests are pass-to-pass). The failing tests cover MultiIndex levels, multi-chunk appends, and a new ValueError with a message the issue does not give.

deciding_assertions: test_pi_sub_pi_length_zero (object result for length-zero PeriodArray subtraction); test_add_length_zero_keeps_dtype and test_add_length_zero_mixed_storage (string dtypes); test_add_length_zero_object_ndarray (pyarrow string + empty object ndarray)
reason: The issue only says that arithmetic on length-zero extension arrays is not tested, with a pint example outside pandas. It names no failing pandas array. The tests need code fixes for Period and string arrays (python and pyarrow storage) that the issue does not identify; adding tests or fixing only a generic path does not pass them.

deciding_assertions: test_sniff_delimiter_small_reads monkeypatches pandas.io.parsers.readers._SNIFF_CHUNK_SIZE; test_sniff_delimiter_multibyte / _lone_surrogate: ValueError match "sep=None detected the separator '\u00a7'"; test_sniff_delimiter_no_rows: EmptyDataError
reason: The issue only asks whether C-engine sniffing could be added. The tests need a new module constant by name, a new error message for multi-byte separators (where a reasonable fix could fall back to python instead), and specific handling of skiprows, comments, mid-stream handles and chunked reads. A reasonable sniffing fix fails at least the _SNIFF_CHUNK_SIZE and message tests.

deciding_assertions: test_column_name_text_missing_raises / test_amd_page_unusable: ValueError match 'refers to text subheader 1'; test_amd_page_unusable: columns[1].format == '\x00\x00\x00\x00    ' fallback; test_amd_page_column_text (format/label refs on amd pages); test_amd_page_zstd; test_amd_page: df.columns[11] == 'TotalNoise'
reason: The issue reports an IndexError on one file and asks that it loads. The tests need column text read from amd pages after the data, a new ValueError with an exact message when text is missing, an exact clamped-format fallback for corrupt pages, and zstd handling. A fix that loads the file (for example by skipping or clamping the bad name reference) fails these.

deciding_assertions: test_stack_duplicate_levels[level0-3]: df.stack(level) raises ValueError with match 'level should not contain duplicate'
reason: The issue offers two options (raise a ValueError, or deduplicate like unstack) and asks maintainers to choose; the test needs option 1. A deduplicating fix fails, and a ValueError fix with any other wording (for example 'duplicate levels are not supported') fails the match.

deciding_assertions: test_join_suffixes_cause_duplicate_columns_deprecated and test_merge_duplicate_suffix: assert_produces_warning(Pandas4Warning, match="Passing 'suffixes' which cause duplicate columns") and the result still has duplicate columns
reason: The issue only asks why join raises without suffixes but accepts suffixes that give duplicate columns; it does not say to warn, deprecate or raise. The natural fix (raise a MergeError, as merge already does for duplicates within one side) fails because the tests need a Pandas4Warning and an unchanged result.

deciding_assertions: test_resample_groupby_agg_listlike_excludes_keys[None/date]: agg(['sum','mean']) equals concat of single-function results; test_groupby_resample_ohlc_empty_excludes_keys: empty-frame groupby.resample.ohlc columns equal the non-empty columns
reason: The list-like agg test follows from the issue (output should match the single-function result), and a fix that excludes the group keys in the agg path passes it, with the on='date' variant medium. The empty-frame ohlc test covers a case the issue never names; a fix limited to the list-like agg path does not change the empty ohlc path and fails it.

deciding_assertions: test_publishes_unserializable: obj._repr_data_resource_() raises NotImplementedError match 'table schema'; 'application/vnd.dataresource+json' not in formatted; also latin-1 bytes (OverflowError) and float16 object (TypeError) cases
reason: The issue asks that the display works with table_schema on; a fix that serializes bytes (for example a default_handler) makes the dataresource output appear and fails the 'not in formatted' check. A fix that returns None or catches only UnicodeDecodeError fails the NotImplementedError match or the OverflowError and TypeError cases, which the issue does not name.

deciding_assertions: test_getitem (resample and rolling): assert_produces_warning(Pandas4Warning, match='Passing a tuple to __getitem__ is deprecated')
reason: The DEPR title and the issue imply a deprecation warning for tuple keys, and a fix in SelectionMixin covers both resample and rolling. The issue gives no message text; a warning with other wording (for example 'Indexing with a tuple is deprecated, use a list') fails the match, and a plain FutureWarning may fail the Pandas4Warning class check.

deciding_assertions: test_query_str_slice_negative_index (the issue's str.slice(0,-1) case) is pass-to-pass; fail-to-pass tests: test_slice_subscript*, test_subscript_non_numeric_key, test_subscript_op_valued, test_multi_dimensional_subscript_raises (NotImplementedError, match 'multi-dimensional subscripts are not supported')
reason: The issue's own query already works before the fix (its test is in pass_to_pass and the comment says so). The failing tests cover subscript slices, variable keys, Op keys and a new NotImplementedError with an exact message, none of which the issue names.

deciding_assertions: test_binary_input_aligns_duplicate_labels / test_binary_ufunc_aligns_duplicate_labels: outer alignment with duplicate labels gives a 3-row result with NaN; test_binary_ufunc_aligns_index_name: result index name equals that of ser1 + ser2
reason: The issue names pandas 1.x as the reference: an element-wise logical op that returns two boolean columns (positional). A fix that restores that behaviour fails the tests, which expect label alignment with NaN rows and columns. The index-name test is a case the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: test_concat_exclude_none, test_concat_keys_with_none, test_concat_preserves_rangeindex[True-*], test_empty_sequence_concat_ok[arg1/arg2]: assert_produces_warning(Pandas4Warning, match='Passing None in the objects to concat is deprecated')
reason: The issue asks to deprecate None in pd.concat but gives no message. A deprecation warning with other wording (for example 'None objects in concat are deprecated') fails the match; the warning class is also a choice.

deciding_assertions: All 3279 fail-to-pass tests are missing before the fix: the test files import PY315 from pandas.compat; test_to_datetime_missing_colon_z_offset and test_to_datetime_colon_z_offset test the %:z directive
reason: The test modules import pandas.compat.PY315, a new name that the issue does not give; without it every test file fails to load. The tests also cover %:z parsing and Python 3.15 message changes that the issue does not mention, and the crash itself needs Python 3.15.

deciding_assertions: test_arrow_array_tz_subtype: pa.array(arr) gives ArrowIntervalType with subtype pa.timestamp(unit, tz), and __arrow_ext_deserialize__(storage_type, __arrow_ext_serialize__()) equals the type; test_arrow_table_roundtrip[tz] and _without_metadata[tz]: round trip gives the same IntervalDtype
reason: The issue asks that pa.array succeeds for a tz-aware interval subtype and that the result round-trips back to the same IntervalDtype, and it says the metadata format must change. Any fix that writes the tz timestamp subtype and restores it on read (by any serialization design) passes these checks; they use only existing names.

deciding_assertions: test_series_repr_float_precision and test_series_repr_float_matches_float64 (interval endpoints formatted like float64, e.g. '(1.000000e-09, 2.000000e-09]', '(0.50, 1.25]'); test_series_repr_float_format; test_float_format_complex_in_object_column; test_float_format_percent_str_complex_in_object_column; test_repr_seq_complex_precision ('[(3.142+1.0j)]')
reason: The issue asks that display.precision applies to complex and tuple values in object columns. The tests also require interval-dtype formatting like float64 (scientific notation, common decimals), float_format applied to complex parts, and exact strings such as '1.0j' for the imaginary part; a fix that applies precision to complex and tuple values fails these cases.

deciding_assertions: test_agg_dict_forwards_kwargs (frame, series, resample, rolling), test_groupby_agg_dict_forwards_args_kwargs, test_agg_mapping_func_deprecated: dict-like agg forwards args and kwargs such as min_count and ddof
reason: The issue reports groupby(axis=1).sum(min_count=1) returning 0 instead of NaN. The tests check that dict-like agg forwards args and kwargs across DataFrame, Series, groupby, resample and rolling, a different code path that the issue does not mention; a fix of the groupby sum min_count case does not touch these.

deciding_assertions: test_max_colwidth_narrower_than_placeholder[0..3]: repr(df) with max_colwidth 0, 1, 2, 3 equals an exact string of partial placeholders ('', '.', '..', '...')
reason: The issue offers two options: raise a ValueError for widths below the placeholder, or show a dot-filled frame. The tests need the second option, with an exact rendering per width (empty cells at 0, one dot at 1). The fix the issue lists first (raise ValueError when the option is set) fails all four tests.

deciding_assertions: test_read_excel_multiindex_header_index_col_consumes_all_columns: read_excel(header=[0,1], index_col=0) on a one-column sheet gives an empty DataFrame with object index and object columns, for every engine
reason: The issue asks for no error and the same result as read_csv, which is an empty frame. The narrowest fix (skip set_names when the parsed columns are empty or their level count does not match) passes; the parser's own empty frame gives the expected object indexes. All engines share the same _parse_sheet path.

deciding_assertions: test_clip_ordered_categorical (series, 5 params; frame): clip bounds are ordered by category position, including swapped bounds ('b','c' with categories a<c<b gives the same as 'c','b'); test_clip_ordered_categorical_bound_not_a_category (passes before): non-category bound raises TypeError 'Invalid comparison'
reason: The issue asks that clip on ordered categoricals use category order; the existing clip swaps scalar bounds so that lower<=upper, and a fix that keeps that swap but orders by category position passes all cases, also the DataFrame entry point and the datetime categories. A fix that only removes the swap for categoricals fails the swapped-bound cases, but it drops existing swap behaviour the issue does not ask to change; the issue's remark on swapping can be read either way.

deciding_assertions: test_from_records_exclude_falsy_label[0, '', False]: exclude=[label] drops the column; test_from_records_index_falsy_label[0, [0]]: index=0 removes column 0 from the columns
reason: The issue names the cause (any(exclude) treats label 0 as false) and the fix (if exclude). That fix passes all cases; '' and False are direct variants of the falsy label 0, and index=0 dropping the column is the stated expected behaviour.

deciding_assertions: test_assert_frame_equal_multiindex_columns_with_na (3 params) and test_assert_frame_equal_groupby_multiindex_columns_with_na: column names ('USD', nan) compare equal; new pass-to-pass tests test_assert_attr_equal_tuple_raising_type_error and test_assert_attr_equal_tuple_nested_type_mismatch: tuples whose elements raise on == or differ in nested sequence type still give AssertionError
reason: The issue asks for an NA-aware comparison inside tuple names. A fix that compares tuples element-wise, treating matching NA as equal and otherwise using ==, passes the frame tests. The two pass-to-pass attr tests only keep existing behaviour (these tuples were reported as different before); a fix that converts tuples to a 2D array or lets a TypeError escape breaks them, so the task is fair but the design has traps.

deciding_assertions: test_converter_unhashable_output_with_na_values (c engine, pass-to-pass): converter output lists/tuples-with-lists must not raise and 'CAT' stays ['CAT'] (the python engine raises here); test_converters_raising_on_empty_field (pass-to-pass): the c engine must still raise when a converter fails on an empty field (the python engine does not, xfail); test_converters_na_values_dtype: re-inference after NA substitution (python engine xfail)
reason: The issue names the python engine as the reference and asks the c engine to match it. Several tests fix behaviour that differs from the python engine: unhashable converter output is tolerated, an empty field is still passed to the converter and raises, and the column dtype is re-inferred. A fix that mirrors the python engine (match na_values against output with a set lookup, or mask NA tokens before the converter) fails at least one of these tests.

deciding_assertions: test_arrowparquet_fsspec_fallback_fails_keeps_pyarrow_error: when both pyarrow and the fsspec fallback fail, the raised error's __cause__ must contain the pyarrow message 'Unable to load libjvm'; test_arrowparquet_oserror_raises (pass-to-pass): non-'hdfs:///' OSErrors must propagate
reason: The issue asks that 'hdfs:///' paths load, as they did with fsspec. The narrowest fix (send 'hdfs:///' paths straight to fsspec, or fall back to fsspec on the pyarrow error) passes the two fallback tests, but it fails the chaining test: either pyarrow is never called, or the fsspec error is raised outside the except block and has no __cause__. Explicit chaining of the pyarrow error is not in the issue.

deciding_assertions: test_subset_rows_column_list_no_temporary_retained[loc-rows, iloc-rows]: df.loc[1:2, cols] and df.iloc[1:3, [0,1,3]] results must not view the (len(cols), len(df)) temporary
reason: The issue reports a single-row lookup and names pandas 2.3.3 as the reference. The facts show that on 2.3.3 the row cases pass and the row-slice cases fail, so the slice cases ask for more than the reference behaviour. The narrowest fix (copy the small result in the scalar-row path) passes loc-row and iloc-row and fails loc-rows and iloc-rows.

deciding_assertions: test_encoding_default_deprecated (sas7bdat, xport): Pandas4Warning with match "The default value of 'encoding' in read_sas is deprecated"; test_encoding_infer_newly_recognized_codes: codes 0 and 28 map to 'cp1252' and 'ascii'; test_encoding_infer_unrecognized_code: inferred_encoding == 'unknown (code=250)'; test_encoding_infer (xport): XportReader._default_encoding; test_encoding_default_deprecated_sas7bdatreader and _header_text_only: warnings also from SAS7BDATReader and for numeric-only files with non-ascii names
reason: The issue asks to deprecate the default and add encoding='infer', but gives no warning text, no mapping for header codes 0 and 28, and no attribute name. The tests need the exact message, the exact code mapping, the new class attribute _default_encoding, and warnings on extra paths (the reader class, header-only text). A correct deprecation with another message or another code mapping fails.

deciding_assertions: test_groupby_categorical_indices_sort_false_multi_key: gb.indices maps each (x, g) key to its own row (key set compared, order not checked); test_groupby_categorical_get_group_sort_false_multi_key: get_group((1, 'mid')) returns row 2
reason: The issue states the wrong pairing of labels and rows and the expected result: indices agree with groups and get_group returns the right rows. Any fix that pairs labels with the right rows (for example building indices from the same codes as groups) passes both tests; the dict key order is not checked.

deciding_assertions: test_complex_median_deprecated and others: Pandas4Warning 'The median of complex data is deprecated'; test_groupby_complex_raises[median, min, max, cummin, rank, ...]: TypeError "dtype 'complex128' does not support operation '...'"; test_complex_reduction_raises[skew, kurt]; test_groupby_complex_var_std_sem; sparse and extension skew/kurt cases
reason: The issue offers two options for groupby median on complex data (raise, or compute the parts separately as Series.median does). The tests need a raise in groupby plus a deprecation warning with an exact message for Series median, and they also cover skew, kurt, var/std/sem, cummin, rank and other reductions that the issue does not name. A fix of either issue option fails many tests.

deciding_assertions: test_multi_index_header_not_increasing (csv engines, fwf), test_multi_index_header_not_increasing_matches_swaplevel, test_read_excel_multiindex_header_not_increasing, test_multiindex_header_not_increasing (html): header=[1, 0] etc. returns columns with levels in the given order (equal to swaplevel of header=[0, 1])
reason: The issue proposes that non-increasing header lists raise a ValueError. The tests instead need non-increasing headers to work, with levels in the order given, across read_csv, read_fwf, read_excel and read_html. The proposed fix (raise ValueError) fails every fail-to-pass test.

deciding_assertions: test_series_from_index[idx1] (RangeIndex): assert not ser._mgr._has_no_reference(0) for Series(idx) and Series(idx, copy=False); test_rangeindex_cached_data: a renamed view idx2 shares the cache, idx is deleted, ser.iloc[0]=99 must leave idx2._data unchanged
reason: The issue's first option, which it proposes, is that Series(RangeIndex) copies the values. That fix leaves the Series with no tracked reference, so the new _has_no_reference assertion fails; the tests need lazy copy-on-write reference tracking instead. A reference-based fix that does not also register views made by _view (rename) fails test_rangeindex_cached_data, a case the issue does not state.

deciding_assertions: test_to_csv_unwritable_url_raises: file://127.0.0.1/... and http://127.0.0.1:1/... must raise ValueError match 'Cannot write to URL'; test_to_csv_file_url: hosts 'localhost'/'LOCALHOST' and a percent-encoded space in the file name; test_to_csv_file_url_query; test_excel_writer_append_file_url (mode 'r+b')
reason: The narrowest reasonable fix makes a write to a file:///path URL go to the local path (or through fsspec) instead of urlopen. It does not raise a ValueError with the exact text 'Cannot write to URL' for http or remote-host file URLs, and it need not handle localhost hosts, percent-decoding, query strings or ExcelWriter append mode. None of these is in the issue.

deciding_assertions: test_mixed_dtype_row_python_scalars[iloc/loc/xs]: under option_context('future.python_scalars', True), the mixed row holds [int, float, bool, int, np.int8] types, row['e'] is the stored np.int8, and the row equals iterrows' row
reason: The issue only asks if the iterrows conversion to Python types is intended and if it should be documented; a natural fix makes iterrows keep NumPy types like iloc does. The tests need the opposite: iloc/loc/xs unbox to Python scalars, only under the option future.python_scalars, which the issue never names, and with special rules for Int64 and object-stored NumPy scalars.

deciding_assertions: test_select_dtypes_masked_name_string_matches_only_masked[Int64/Int32/Float64/boolean]: include='Int64' selects only the masked column and exclude='Int64' keeps only the numpy column
reason: The narrowest reasonable fix makes an Arrow dtype string ('timestamp[ns][pyarrow]') match like the equivalent ArrowDtype instance, which passes the Arrow timestamp test and the int64/float64/bool [pyarrow] string tests. The masked-dtype tests check nullable names such as 'Int64', a different dtype family that the issue does not mention, and an Arrow-only fix still matches the numpy int64 column through dtype.type and fails them.

deciding_assertions: test_assert_almost_equal_large_mixed_integer_float_message: str(error) == 'expected 1152921504606846976.00000 but got 1152921504606846977.00000, with rtol=0, atol=0.5'
reason: A reasonable fix skips the array_equivalent shortcut for int/float pairs and compares the exact integer values; it passes the atol/rtol tests for scalars, arrays, uint64, Int64/Float64 and assert_series_equal. The message test needs the integer printed exactly. A fix that keeps the existing float-formatted message prints 2**60+1 as ...976.00000, which the issue does not ask to change, and fails it.

deciding_assertions: test_get_locs_too_many_levels / _loc / _reports_full_length: KeyError match 'Key length \(3\) exceeds index depth \(2\)' (length 4 with a trailing slice(None)); test_get_locs_too_many_levels_ellipsis[0]: NotImplementedError before the lexsort check; test_get_loc_level_too_many_levels; test_slice_locs_too_many_levels
reason: The issue asks for an error that says the key has more entries than the index has levels, but gives no error class or text. A reasonable fix in get_locs could raise IndexingError('Too many indexers') or a ValueError and fail the KeyError match. The tests also cover get_loc_level, slice_locs, the Ellipsis order and the counting of trailing null slices, which the issue does not state.

deciding_assertions: test_to_string_numeric_multiindex_columns_alignment[True/False]: MultiIndex columns with numeric levels [0,0]/[0,100] render like string labels
reason: The narrowest reasonable fix stops padding flat numeric column labels to a common width; it passes the flat int64/Int64/float64 tests and the changed truncation expectations. The MultiIndex-column tests check a separate formatting path that the issue does not show, and a fix of the flat path alone fails them.

deciding_assertions: test_interp_large_integer_index_precision: plain int64/uint64 indexes near 2**60 and 2**63, including [-(2**60), 2**60, 0, 1, 3] which must not be shifted; test_interp_ns_index_precision with method='krogh' and a TimedeltaIndex start
reason: The issue is about DatetimeIndex interpolation losing precision. A reasonable fix shifts datetime-like i8 values toward zero before the float cast, and passes the index/values/time cases. The tests also need plain integer indexes, which the issue does not mention, and the zero-spanning case fails a fix that always shifts by the minimum. So only one particular design passes.

deciding_assertions: test_to_timedelta_subint64_with_unit_object_path (list inputs), test_to_timedelta_narrow_float_with_unit (float16/float32), test_unit_subint64_scalars / test_unit_narrow_float_scalars / test_unit_float_neg_inf_raises (to_datetime), test_to_datetime_month_or_year_unit_int with numpy ints, test_to_datetime_narrow_float_with_format_no_runtime_warning
reason: The issue's scalar case to_timedelta(np.int32(0), 'D') is not in the fail-to-pass list, and the existing test_to_timedelta_subint64_with_unit already checks the scalar Timedelta path. The tests check the object-array path, to_datetime, float16/float32 precision, float16 -inf against the NaT sentinel, and a RuntimeWarning in strptime, none of which the issue states.

deciding_assertions: test_to_integer_array_from_masked_out_of_range (array/_from_sequence of a masked Int64 array, values behind the mask ignored); test_setitem_masked_array_out_of_bounds_behind_mask; test_unsafe_integer_dtype_raises_for_non_int64_source (uint64-overflow and float sources, ValueError); test_out_of_range_integer_dtype_raises for numpy int8/uint8 and the python engine
reason: The narrowest reasonable fix makes read_csv with a nullable integer dtype raise the cast error that the Series constructor gives; it passes the UInt8/Int8 parser cases. The tests also need masked-array casting and setitem behind the mask, numpy int8/uint8 dtypes, and uint64 or float parsed sources to raise with a specific ValueError text. The issue and its pandas 1.5.3 reference do not state these cases.

deciding_assertions: test_construct_from_tzaware_warns (scalar Period with a tz-aware string, Timestamp or datetime warns 'drop timezone'); test_period_index_from_tzaware_warns_once (exactly one warning); TestPeriodConverter::test_conversion warns; test_tzaware_warns for period_range
reason: The issue offers two options: tz-aware PeriodIndex (preferred) or a warning; the tests need the warning, so the preferred option fails. The issue also says to fix this in the PeriodIndex constructor, but the tests need the warning from the scalar Period constructor and the plotting converter too, and exactly one warning for an array.

deciding_assertions: test_valid_tolerance and test_tolerance_negative_one_nanosecond: pytest.raises(MergeError, match='tolerance must be non-negative') for negative tolerances
reason: The issue gives the exact new message 'tolerance must be non-negative'. The narrowest fix changes the three messages to that text and passes both tests; test_tolerance_zero already passes before the fix and keeps passing.

deciding_assertions: test_cellstyle_rules_split_at_8192_selectors[map, map_index_0, map_index_1]: 8193 styled cells or labels give exactly [8192, 1] selectors per rule
reason: The issue reports that styles stop showing in Chrome and Edge for large frames but never names a selector limit. A fix that splits rules at another size, or writes styles in another way, fails the exact [8192, 1] assertion. The map_index cases (index label styles) are also not in the issue.

deciding_assertions: test_stack_na_label_lookup: after future stack, result.loc[(NA, 'a')] finds the NA label, isin counts it once, and unstack puts the NA label first (labels.take([1, 0, 2]))
reason: The issue is an open discussion about None in indices and says the author does not know the best solution; it proposes no behaviour. It never mentions stack, label lookup after stack, or the order of NA labels after unstack, so a fix made from the issue cannot target these assertions.

deciding_assertions: test_astype_dt64_to_sparse_int64_fill_value[dtype1]: SparseDtype('int64') (default fill 0) must give fill iNaT, also through Series.astype; test_astype_fully_dense_na_fill_to_int_no_raise: fully dense float SparseArray with NaN fill astype 'Sparse[int64]' must not raise
reason: The issue says the author expected the NaT fill conversion to Sparse[int64] to raise, while the tests expect iNaT, and an explicit SparseDtype('int64') with fill 0 must be treated as not explicit, which is a design choice the issue does not give. The fully dense float case is not in the issue; a fix that only extends the existing string path to SparseDtype objects still raises there.

deciding_assertions: test_shares_memory_arrow_chunked, _arrow_nested, _arrow_no_buffers, _masked, _multiindex: new behaviour of tm.shares_memory (any chunk, None and empty buffers, masked vs ndarray, every MultiIndex code level)
reason: The issue only asks to add tests for tm.shares_memory and asks for no behaviour change. The fail-to-pass tests need several behaviour changes in shares_memory that the issue never states, so a fix that adds tests or leaves the helper as it is fails them.

deciding_assertions: test_read_csv_line_break_as_separator: re.escape match of a new message '... To parse '\n' as a separator, pass a lineterminator other than '\n' (engine='c' only).'; test_parallel_read helper calls _refine_defaults_read(..., lineterminator=...)
reason: Allowing a newline separator with a custom lineterminator follows from the issue, but the tests also need an exact extended error message that the issue does not give, and a new lineterminator keyword of the private helper _refine_defaults_read. A fix that keeps the old message or passes the lineterminator another way fails these tests.

deciding_assertions: test_corr_nearly_constant: corr equals -1.0 for the issue data; test_corr_constant_inexact_mean: corr of [0.1]*3 with [0, 1, 2] is NaN
reason: The issue asks only that Pearson correlation stay within [-1, 1]; the code before the fix already clips the result with np.clip, so the stated case already works. The tests instead need an exact -1.0 for two points that differ by 1 ulp and NaN for a constant series with an inexact mean, which the issue does not ask for.

deciding_assertions: test_datetime_object_epoch_matches_datetime64: object datetimes before 1970 must floor like datetime64 for s/ms/us, and datetime(3000, 1, 1) must serialize in s/ms/us without overflow
reason: The narrowest fix adds the nanosecond part of Timestamp objects and passes test_timestamp_nanoseconds_preserved. It does not change the epoch rounding of pre-1970 object datetimes or the overflow for dates outside the nanosecond range, which the issue (about iso output losing nanoseconds) never mentions, so it fails test_datetime_object_epoch_matches_datetime64.

deciding_assertions: test_epoch_out_of_bounds_for_date_unit and _labels: pytest.raises(OverflowError, match='Datetime value is out of bounds for the requested date_unit')
reason: The category and sparse equality tests follow from the issue's stated expectation. But the out-of-bounds tests need a specific error class and a new exact message for overflow when scaling to a finer unit, which the issue does not mention; a correct fix that raises another error or message fails them.

deciding_assertions: test_pickle.py imports to_pickle_internal from pandas.io.pickle (all 777 tests missing before the fix); test_to_pickle_deprecated expects Pandas4Warning matching 'pandas.to_pickle is deprecated'
reason: The issue asks whether to deprecate pandas.to_pickle or to document it, so it offers two options. The test module only loads when a new function named to_pickle_internal exists, a name the issue never gives, and the deprecation message and warning class are also not given.

deciding_assertions: test_subclass_name_with_explicit_name: name='public_name' must give 'SubBar.public_name'; test_keyword_deprecation (to_string, to_markdown): message must say 'Series.to_string' and 'Series.to_markdown' where the decorators pass explicit name=
reason: test_subclass_name follows from the issue. But the issue says nothing about an explicit name argument; a reasonable fix that keeps the given name unchanged (existing behaviour) fails the explicit-name test and the to_string and to_markdown tests, which need the class prepended to explicit names or the name arguments removed.

deciding_assertions: test_to_datetime_categorical_container[51-*]: to_datetime of a Categorical, a CategoricalIndex and a categorical Series with 51 rows equals the DatetimeIndex/Series that the uncached (50-row) path gives; test_to_datetime_categorical_all_coerced[51]: all-NaT coerced result is M8[s] DatetimeIndex/Series, as at 50 rows
reason: The issue asks that the result type not flip when the cache starts at 51 rows. The narrowest reasonable fix makes the cached path return what the uncached path returns (for example cast the mapped result to the cache dtype, or convert the categories and take). Every expected value is the uncached result at 50 rows; the Series and CategoricalIndex inputs and the all-coerced case are direct variants of the same consistency rule.

deciding_assertions: test_duplicated_subset[*-subset3]: df.duplicated(subset=[]) equals df[[]].duplicated(), which is all False; test_drop_duplicates_empty_subset: drop_duplicates(subset=[]) returns the frame unchanged
reason: The issue states that duplicated() on a frame with no selected columns should give [False, True, True, ...], because all rows are equal. A fix of subset=[] that follows that stated output returns False for the first row and True for the rest, and drop_duplicates then keeps one row; both tests expect all False and the full frame. Only a fix that copies the current all-False result of df[[]].duplicated() passes.

deciding_assertions: test_can_use_numexpr_pow: expr._can_use_numexpr(operator.pow, '**', arr, other, 'evaluate') returns False for int64 with 2 and np.int64(2), and True for int64 with 2.0 and for float64 with int exponents
reason: The issue asks that integer pow give the same result with numexpr as plain numpy. A reasonable fix that routes integer pow to numpy in _evaluate_numexpr, in evaluate(), or that disables numexpr for pow whenever the left operand is an integer passes test_integer_pow_matches_numpy and the negative-exponent test, but fails the direct assertions on the internal _can_use_numexpr return value (including the int64 ** 2.0 -> True case).

deciding_assertions: test_string_index_real_na_roundtrips_fixed/_table, test_string_index_real_na_and_literal_nan_roundtrip, test_string_index_all_na_roundtrips: a real NaN in a str Index round-trips as NaN in HDF5
reason: The issue reports that the literal string 'nan' in an index is read back as NaN. The repo already handles that: pass-to-pass tests test_string_nan_in_index_fixed/_table exist, and the string index reader already passes nan_rep=None. The new tests check the opposite direction (a real missing value must come back as NaN, with a collision-free sentinel stored in the file), which the issue does not ask for.

deciding_assertions: test_str_extract_non_symbolic[expand], _non_symbolic_multiple, _mixed_symbolic, _non_symbolic_flags, _mixed_symbolic_flags: ArrowDtype str.extract labels unnamed groups by position, named by name, non-matches as null, with and without flags
reason: The issue lists these exact patterns and gives the expected frames: unnamed groups labelled by position, mixable with named ones, also with flags, matching other dtypes. The narrowest reasonable fix (send any pattern with an unnamed group to the re fallback and label by _get_group_names) passes every assertion; the expand=False case is the normal single-group behaviour of other dtypes.

deciding_assertions: test_shift_with_array_like_periods_series[periods0-3]: Series.shift with np.array([0]), Index([0]), Series([0]) or np.array([0, 1]) equals df.shift(list(periods)); also test_shift_with_int_periods_series_suffix_raises
reason: The issue only says that suffix is ignored in Series.shift. The narrowest reasonable fix passes suffix to the to_frame().shift call, which passes test_shift_with_iterable_series_suffix (and the raise test follows from DataFrame.shift). It does not fix the separate bug where array-like periods hit the 'periods == 0' check (unshifted copy or ambiguous truth value), so the four array-like tests fail.

deciding_assertions: test_to_excel_multiindex_values_format_identically[True-*]: to_excel with merge_cells round-trips two index values that format the same; test_rowspan_values_format_identically: Styler.to_html has no rowspan for [1, '1']; test_to_string_multiindex_sparsify_by_value: also the column MultiIndex of df.T
reason: The issue reports the notebook display (to_html repr) merging distinct float index values that format the same. A reasonable fix in the HTML/string formatter, or one that adds codes to sparsify_labels only for the index path, fixes the issue case and to_html but fails the Excel merge_cells test, the Styler test, or the column-axis to_string check. Only a fix at the shared MultiIndex sparsify step, also applied to the columns call, passes all.

deciding_assertions: test_transform_udf_scalar_extension_dtype_column: Int64 column with an NA first value comes back as object; test_transform_udf_scalar_user_defined_class: non-scalar Box result keeps 'a' int and 'b' object; new tests test_transform_udf_scalar_none_is_nan (None -> float NaN) and test_transform_udf_scalar_same_dtypes_uses_fast_path (last call gets a 2D frame)
reason: The issue case (int and float columns keep their dtypes) is checked by test_transform_udf_reduction_keeps_column_dtypes, which any per-column fix passes. The other tests fix edge behaviours that the issue does not state: a fix that casts results back to the original column dtypes gives Int64, not object; a fix that detects mixed dtypes with lib.is_scalar misses Box; a fix that builds a frame from the scalars leaves None as an object column; a fix that always goes column by column loses the fast path.

deciding_assertions: test_encode_error_not_masked_by_sibling[*], test_to_json_error_not_masked_by_sibling: complex then plain object must raise 'is not JSON serializable'; test_encode_failure_frees_grown_buffer: tracemalloc growth < 100000; test_to_json_bad_label_frees_values: values array is freed; test_encode_object_dir_non_str: match 'must return str entries, not int'; test_encode_set_iter_raises_midway
reason: The issue lists the unchecked API calls (lone surrogates in keys, dir and labels, large int keys, raising __dir__ and set __iter__) and its unit tests match several hidden tests. A fix that checks those calls passes them, but fails the tests on a sibling object clearing a pending exception, on buffer and reference leaks after a failed encode, and on the exact new message for non-str __dir__ entries, none of which the issue states.

deciding_assertions: test_read_workbook_infers_engine[odf-*], [pyxlsb-*], [calamine-*]: ExcelFile/read_excel infer the engine from odf OpenDocument, pyxlsb Workbook and CalamineWorkbook objects
reason: The issue asks only that an openpyxl.Workbook imply engine='openpyxl', and proposes exactly that check. The narrowest reasonable fix (the issue's own proposal) passes the openpyxl case but fails the odf, pyxlsb and calamine workbook cases, which the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: test_inconsistent_number_of_rows: load_log has 2088 rows; test_deleted_rows[chunksize-last_on_page]: deleted rows on mix and data pages skipped, also across chunks and at page end; test_deleted_rows_other_layouts: synthetic deleted rows in x86 and big-endian files (pointer at page offset 12 for x86, 24 for x64; MSB-first bitmap after the rows)
reason: The issue asks that rows SAS marks deleted are not returned. A correct general fix must implement the SAS page format for deleted rows (page flag, bitmap located by a pointer after the rows, one bit per row); the x64 layout and bit order can be checked against the repo's load_log file, and chunked reading and other byte orders are direct variants. Doubt: the x86 pointer offset 12 is tested only on synthetic files and comes from format knowledge, not the issue; a fix that guessed another x86 offset fails those cases.

deciding_assertions: test_assert_almost_equal_iterable_length_mismatch_unhashable: list/tuple-with-list/array/dict element vs [1, 2] raises AssertionError whose message is exactly the existing 'Iterable length are different' text with no [diff] line; test_assert_equal_nested_list_length_mismatch: Series/DataFrame of the issue case raise 'values are different (33.33333 %)' with 'At positional index 1, first diff: ...'
reason: The issue asks for the normal AssertionError instead of TypeError on unhashable nested elements. The narrowest fix catches the TypeError of the set-based diff in testing.pyx and skips the diff, which gives the existing no-diff message and passes the anchored match and the frame/series test; the unhashable variants (tuple with list, array, dict) are direct variants. A fix that invents a new diff format for unhashable elements would fail the anchored message, so a reader could see this as a design choice.

deciding_assertions: test_constructor_non_integer_codes_raises: ValueError with match='MultiIndex codes must be integers' for NaN, 0.5 and inf codes, in list, float array and object array, through the constructor and set_codes
reason: The issue asks that NaN codes in a NumPy array raise 'the same ValueError' as the list case ('cannot convert float NaN to integer'). The narrowest fix raises that existing error for NaN in arrays, which fails the new message match, also for the list case that already raised; 0.5 and inf codes and set_codes are not stated in the issue.

deciding_assertions: test_categorical_append_different_categories_dtype: appending float categories [1.0, 2.0, 4.0] after int categories [1, 2, 3] raises ValueError matching 'cannot append a categorical with different categories to the existing'
reason: The test is the issue's own example, and the issue gives the expected error class and message (the 3.0.6 behaviour). Any fix that makes validate_metadata compare the categories without the Cython dtype error, and treats them as different, passes.

deciding_assertions: test_sum_timedelta64_overflow_raises: DataFrame.sum (axis 0/1, skipna True/False) raises pd.errors.OutOfBoundsTimedelta matching 'overflow in timedelta operation'; test_sum_timedelta64_all_nat_skipna_false and test_td64_sum_all_nat_skipna_false: all-NaT sum with skipna=False returns NaT
reason: The issue asks that Series x*2 raise and that all overflow errors be OverflowError. The tests do not check x*2; they check DataFrame.sum overflow with OutOfBoundsTimedelta (a ValueError, not the OverflowError the issue asks for) and a specific message, and all-NaT reductions with skipna=False that the issue never mentions. A fix of the issue's cases (raise OverflowError on multiplication overflow, unify sum errors as OverflowError) fails these tests.

deciding_assertions: Test modules (test_arrow, test_to_datetime, test_parsing, test_to_time, test_between_time) use the new decorator td.skip_if_not_english_lc_time; all 28465 fail-to-pass tests are missing before the fix because the modules fail to load

deciding_assertions: test_skipfooter_counts_discarded_lines (issue case, passes with a fix of the issue); test_skipfooter_counts_skiprows_lines (python and read_fwf) and test_skipfooter_counts_skiprows_lines_data_list: skiprows=[4] inside the footer with skipfooter=2 must give rows 1,3,5
reason: The issue shows blank and comment lines consumed during header inference not being counted by skipfooter, with skiprows only at the top of the file. Three of four fail-to-pass tests check a different case: a skiprows line that falls inside the footer, which before the fix was removed before skipfooter was counted. A reasonable fix that counts the discarded blank/comment lines passes the issue case but not these tests; only a fix that cuts by raw file line number covers both.

deciding_assertions: test_series_groupby_as_index_false_name_collision: group label named like the Series raises ValueError 'cannot insert val, already exists' for sum, quantile, apply, value_counts; test_series_groupby_as_index_false_keys with Series name 'index': result must equal reset_index (key column 'level_0')
reason: The issue proposes to_frame plus _insert_inaxis_grouper_inplace plus a range index. That existing helper silently skips inserting a key whose name is already a column, so the issue's own design returns no error on a name collision and drops the key column when the Series is named 'index'. The tests require reset_index semantics (raise on collision, rename to level_0), which the issue does not state.

deciding_assertions: test_to_dense_keeps_categories_dtype and test_to_dense_with_missing: Categorical.to_dense keeps the categories dtype with specific upcasts for missing values; test_cat_accessor_to_dense, test_getname_categorical_accessor[to_dense], test_tab_completion_with_categorical: Series.cat.to_dense exists
reason: The issue is an open API question: whether to add some new method that keeps the dtype, and whether to deprecate to_dense. The tests require one option (change to_dense itself), expose it on the .cat accessor (not mentioned), and fix the missing-value upcast rules. A fix that adds a differently named method, or deprecates to_dense, fails.

deciding_assertions: test_short_line_run_at_chunk_boundary[c_low-4] (issue case: multi-row header, short lines across a low_memory chunk boundary); test_bad_line_first_in_chunk (8 tests): with header=None and chunksize 1 or 2, a too-long line in buffer slot 0 must raise 'Expected 3 fields' or be skipped
reason: The issue reports short lines (missing delimiters) that raise ParserError with header=[0,1] and low_memory=True. A fix that stops the header-slot exemption after the header (so short lines are padded) passes the short-line test, but 8 of 9 fail-to-pass tests check a separate bug: too-long lines after a chunk boundary escaping on_bad_lines with chunksize and header=None, which the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: test_default_format_year_lt_1000 (Period str/strftime(None) zero-pads year for 8 freqs); test_strftime_fiscal_year_lt_1000 (%F gives '0020'); test_repr_year_lt_1000 (Timestamp repr '0020-...'); test_strftime_dt64_default_formats_year_lt_1000 (negative year formatted '-020-01-01')
reason: The issue proposes a new engine parameter ('pystr', 'os', 'auto') for strftime; the tests do not use it and instead require zero-padding of the year in default fast paths, a behaviour the issue does not choose (it notes padding differs by OS). The exact '-020' for a negative year, and Period and Timestamp repr cases, are not given in the issue.

deciding_assertions: test_copy_owns_buffers_special_layouts (string_view, binary_view), test_copy_owns_nested_buffers (list/struct with dictionary or string_view child), test_copy_owns_extension_storage_buffers (json_ extension with string_view storage): the copy must not share these buffers
reason: The issue asks that a deep copy of an arrow-backed array not keep the original buffers alive. The narrowest fix makes ArrowExtensionArray.copy use the existing _copy_pyarrow_buffers (or pa.concat_arrays); it passes the basic copy tests but not the view-type, nested dictionary/view and extension-storage tests, because concat_arrays reuses those buffers. These layouts are not mentioned in the issue.

deciding_assertions: should work with glob: urlMatches with globs 'http://example.com:80/path', 'https://example.com:443/path', 'http://localhost:80/**', 'http://example.com/foo bar', 'http://münchen.de/' match the normalized URLs; the :8080 case keeps working.
reason: The issue names all three regressed cases (default port, percent-encoding, IDN host) and the 1.50 reference behaviour, and proposes the fix. The narrowest reasonable fix (pass glob components without metacharacters through new URL() unchanged) makes every new assertion pass and keeps the existing glob assertions.

deciding_assertions: serial suites expose a serial annotation for custom sharding: each test in preprocess has N annotations of type 'serial' (0, 1, 1, 2 for nesting); static modifiers should be added in serial mode: annotations start with { type: 'serial', location: {line: 0, column: 0} }.
reason: The issue asks for the test groups in the public API, for example testRun.groups(). The tests instead expect a new annotation type 'serial' on each test, one per serial ancestor suite. A fix that adds testRun.groups() as the issue proposes fails both tests.

deciding_assertions: parseLocator round-trips mixed role options: parseLocator(lang, asLocator(lang, sel)) === sel for checked=mixed and pressed=mixed in javascript, python, java, csharp.
reason: The issue gives both options, all four languages and the expected round trip. The narrowest reasonable fix (accept the string 'mixed' besides booleans for checked and pressed in getByRoleParts) passes every assertion.

deciding_assertions: should fill datetime-local input: fill '2020-03-02T06:20:00' gives input.value '2020-03-02T06:20'; fill '2020-03-02T05:15' still works.
reason: The issue gives the case and the browser normalization to the value without zero seconds. Any reasonable fix (relax the equality check for datetime-local, or drop it) passes; the old throw tests are removed in the test change, so a fix that keeps the Malformed value checks for other types also passes.

deciding_assertions: should not turn complete clone shallow when capturing diff: gitDiff contains the file and is-shallow-repository is 'false'; should fetch missing pull request base commit when capturing diff: base commit only on origin, gitDiff contains 'baseline.txt' and the clone stays complete.
reason: The issue asks that a complete clone stays complete and suggests skipping --depth=1 when the repo is not shallow. That fix still fetches the missing base commit, so both tests pass; a fix that also skips the fetch when the base exists passes too. Dropping the fetch for complete clones would break existing behaviour, so it is not a reasonable fix.

deciding_assertions: session stops when temporary socket directory disappears: with no opt-in option, after the TMPDIR socket folder is renamed, the daemon process must exit.
reason: The issue asks for an opt-in lifecycle (idle timeout, lease or owner watch) and says default behaviour can stay unchanged. The test expects the daemon to stop by default when its socket path disappears. An opt-in --idle-timeout or lease, as the issue proposes, fails the test.

deciding_assertions: reverse engineer internal:role with regex and string name/description: regex name + string description and string name + regex description generate getByRole code in javascript, python, java and csharp.
reason: The issue gives both combinations, says the other languages are affected too, and names the cause (regex counted in the exactness check). The narrowest fix (only string values take part in the exactness check) gives the expected output, which follows from the existing generators.

deciding_assertions: find --max-results truncates output / browser_find maxResults option: header 'Found 3 matches for /Fruit/ (showing first 2):'; --max-results=0, -1, 1.5 give '"maxResults" must be a positive integer.'
reason: The issue names --max-results but gives no truncation notice text and no validation message. A fix that limits the results with another header (or none) or another error text fails these assertions.

deciding_assertions: should gracefully close the browser once on stdin end: stderr with DEBUG=pw:browser has '<gracefully close start>' and '<gracefully close end>', and no '<forcefully close>' or '<will force kill>'.
reason: The test checks the issue's own expected result with the log lines the issue shows. Both fixes the issue suggests (a second gracefullyClose waits for the first, or one owner for the stdin EOF shutdown) avoid the force branch and so pass. The test is timing based, so I cannot be fully sure for every design.

deciding_assertions: cdp.spec 'transparently reconnects when the remote browser is restarted' and launch.spec 'isolated context relaunches the browser after it dies': wait for stderr 'browser disconnected' (pw:mcp:backend), then the next tool call must reconnect.
reason: The issue is only about extension mode relay reconnect. Both fail-to-pass tests cover CDP endpoint mode and isolated launch mode, and they wait for a new debug message 'browser disconnected'. A fix in cdpRelay.ts that reopens the connect page, as the issue suggests, passes neither.

deciding_assertions: should append node error code to the message: message contains 'socket hang up (ECONNRESET)'; should expose node error fields on network errors: error.syscall === 'read' and typeof error.errno === 'number'.
reason: The issue asks to keep the structured fields, 'at minimum err.code'. A fix that copies only code fails the syscall and errno assertions, and no reasonable fix of the issue appends ' (ECONNRESET)' to the message in that exact form.

deciding_assertions: should use configured webp type: config expect.toHaveScreenshot.type: 'webp'; should fail on unsupported configured type: output contains 'config.expect.toHaveScreenshot.type must be one of "png" or "webp"'.
reason: The issue proposes the option name screenshotFormat; the tests use the new name 'type' and an exact validation message. A fix that adds screenshotFormat as the issue shows fails both tests.

deciding_assertions: should load css imports as empty modules in esm: a loader registered in the config handles './hello.txt' (text === 'hello'), and css imports still give {}.
reason: The issue proposes to pass extensions that Playwright does not transform to nextLoad(); .txt is a direct variant of .mdx. The narrowest fix (delegate unknown extensions in the load hook, keep the style file handling) passes. Medium because the test depends on which loader mode the run uses.

deciding_assertions: should update host header on redirect: request sent with header key 'HosT' must have its host updated on redirect so the redirected request reaches the target with redirectCount 2 and an OK response
reason: The issue names the exact bug (case-sensitive 'host' lookup on redirect) and proposes a case-insensitive lookup. The narrowest fix, the issue's own suggested change, finds the 'HosT' key and updates it, so the test passes.

deciding_assertions: negative number arguments: cli('mousewheel','-.5') must give the error "'dy' argument: expected number, received 'undefined'", so '-.5' must be parsed as a positional argument
reason: The issue's case 'mousewheel 0 -100' passes with the issue's suggested fix, treating args that match /^-\d/ as positional. That fix still parses '-.5' as a short flag, so the run fails with 'Unknown options' and not with the expected 'dy' error. A negative number without a leading digit is a variant the issue does not state.

deciding_assertions: should match text snapshot with trailing newline difference: 'Hello world' vs file 'Hello world\n' and 'Hello world\n' vs file 'Hello world' must both match (exit code 0)
